title: One-Pot Creamy Tomato, White Bean & Orzo
description: Orzo, white beans, and tomatoes simmer together into a creamy pantry-friendly one-pot dinner.
substitutions: Use great northern, cannellini, or navy beans.
Use small pasta such as ditalini instead of orzo and adjust simmer time as needed.
Stir in a handful of spinach at the end if you have some.

steps.text: Simmer the orzo, beans, and tomatoes.

cookSteps.text: Combine 1 cup dry orzo, 1 can drained white beans, 1 can diced tomatoes, 2 1/2 cups broth, and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder in a large saucepan or deep skillet.
Bring to a boil, reduce to a steady simmer, and cook 10–12 minutes, stirring often, until the orzo is tender and most of the liquid is absorbed.
Stir in 1/2 cup milk and cook 2–3 minutes more over low heat until creamy.
Stir in up to 1/2 cup shredded Parmesan or mozzarella if using. Taste, season if needed, and serve.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Add a splash of milk, broth, or water when reheating because the orzo thickens as it sits.

title: Turkey, Apple & Cheddar Pinwheels
description: Deli turkey, crisp apple, and cheddar roll into tortillas for a fast no-cook lunch or light dinner.
substitutions: Use deli ham instead of turkey.
Use sliced cheddar instead of shredded cheddar.
Use a little mustard instead of cream cheese or mayonnaise if you like.

cookSteps.text: Lay out 2 large tortillas and spread each with 1 tablespoon cream cheese or mayonnaise if using.
Divide 6 ounces deli turkey, 1 thinly sliced small apple, and 3/4 cup shredded cheddar evenly between the tortillas, keeping the fillings away from one edge.
Roll each tortilla tightly toward the bare edge. Slice each roll into pinwheels or leave whole as a wrap and serve.

storage: Best eaten the day they are made. Wrap tightly and refrigerate up to 24 hours; the apple will soften slightly.

title: Leftover Roasted Potato & Broccoli Egg Hash
description: Leftover roasted potatoes and broccoli turn into a crisp skillet hash with eggs for an easy food-rescue breakfast or dinner.

ingredients.item: leftover roasted potatoes and broccoli, chopped

substitutions: Use any cooked potato plus leftover roasted vegetables.
Scramble the eggs into the hash instead of cooking them on top.
Use Monterey Jack or mozzarella instead of cheddar.

steps.text: Cook eggs on top and finish with cheese.

cookSteps.text: Heat 1 tablespoon oil or butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add 2 cups chopped leftover roasted potatoes and broccoli plus 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder if using.
Cook 4–5 minutes, stirring only once or twice, until hot and crisp at the edges.
Make 4 small spaces in the hash and crack 1 egg into each. Reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and cook 3–5 minutes, until the egg whites are set to your liking.
Sprinkle with up to 1/2 cup shredded cheddar if using, cover for about 1 minute to melt, then serve.

storage: Best fresh. Refrigerate leftovers up to 2 days and reheat until hot; fully cooked eggs reheat best.

title: Small-Batch Cinnamon Pear Oat Muffins
description: One ripe pear and pantry oats make a small batch of soft cinnamon muffins without leaving a dozen extras behind.
substitutions: Use a small apple instead of pear.
Use quick oats instead of old-fashioned oats.
Add 2 tablespoons raisins if you want extra sweetness.

steps.text: Mix the dry and wet ingredients.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 375°F and grease or line 6 muffin cups. Mix 3/4 cup flour, 1/2 cup oats, 1/3 cup brown sugar, 1 teaspoon baking powder, and 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon in a bowl.
Whisk 1 egg, 1/3 cup milk, and 3 tablespoons melted butter or oil together. Stir the wet mixture into the dry ingredients just until combined, then fold in 1 finely diced ripe pear.
Divide the batter among 6 muffin cups and bake 18–20 minutes, until the tops spring back and a tester comes out without wet batter.
Cool in the pan 5 minutes, then move the muffins to a rack or plate.

storage: Keep covered at room temperature up to 2 days or refrigerate up to 5 days. Freeze up to 2 months.
